content:
You are an AI model embedded in a custom harness. You are running on the users machine.

You will encounter system, model and author prompts. System prompts result from tool callings or general context,
model prompts are from you, and user prompts are directly from the user.

Tool calls are possible. To know which tools are available, use the "list-tools" tool. Any tool you want to invoke
must be specified by the "list-tools" tool, otherwise it is not present. To invoke a tool, write use json syntax
of the form {"tool":<tool-id>,"args":<args>} where <args> is a string of a specific syntax specified by the tool.
The object should be as trimmed as possible, no unnecessary whitespaces. Every tool call from you must be wrapped within
a leading and following new line, aka 
<tool-call>
.
author: system

content: tell me a joke
author: user

content:
Why did the scarecrow win an award? 

Because he was outstanding in his field!

content:
Tool list-tools -- 1/4
  The "list-tools" tool can be used to list all tools available. It returns the description
of all tools, explaining what they are used for, and what there syntax is.

To invoke, respond in the form of {tool:"list-tools",args:""}. No arguments other then "" are possible.
Tool read-file -- 2/4
  The "read-file" tool can be used to read the contents of any file provided its path.
Bulk operations are possible, one can supply multiple file paths to get the contents at once.

To invoke, respond in the form of {tool:"read-file",args:string[]} where the string array are
the paths to requested files. Absolute as well as relative file paths are possible.
Tool list-dir -- 3/4
  The "list-dir" tool can be used to list the contents of a directory provided its path.
Bulk operations are possible, one can supply multiple directory paths to get the contents at once.

To invoke, respond in the form of {"tool":"list-dir","args":string[]} where the string array are
the paths to requested directories. Absolute as well as relative directory paths are possible.
Tool write-file -- 4/4
  The "write-file" tool can be used to create new files or overwrite existing files with provided content.
It acts on one file at a time.

To invoke, respond in the form of {"tool":"write-file","args":{"path":"string","content":"string"}} where path is the target file path and content is the string content to write. Absolute as well as relative file paths are possible.

content:
Here is a list of all the files in the `src` folder along with a summary of their purpose:

### Core / Root (`src/`)
* **`constants.ts`**: Defines core types such as `Message` and `Author`, and stores shared constants like the timestamp formatter and the initial `SYSTEM_PROMPT` for the AI model.
* **`index.ts`**: The main application entry point. It sets up a new conversation session, listens for user input from the terminal (`Deno.stdin`), passes it to the AI, and outputs the responses using the logger.

### Utilities (`src/coder/`)
* **`conversations.ts`**: Contains helper functions to create structured messages (adding unique IDs and timestamps) and to filter conversations by specific authors (like extracting only the model's messages).
* **`logger.ts`**: A utility class that formats and prints conversation messages to the console with color-coded tags and timestamps. 
* **`tools.ts`**: Provides the `extractTools` function, which parses the AI's raw text responses to detect tool invocations and returns the corresponding executable tool instances.

### AI Harness & Logic (`src/harness/`)
* **`feed.ts`**: Contains the core AI loop. It prompts the language model with the conversation history, extracts any requested tool calls, executes them, and automatically feeds the tool results back into the model for follow-up responses.
* **`models.ts`**: Initializes and exports the different Google Gemini AI models (via `@ai-sdk/google`) used by the system, configured with the `AI_STUDIO_API_KEY` environment variable.
* **`session.ts`**: Defines the `Session` class, which manages the state of an ongoing chat. It handles keeping track of the conversation history, routing messages to the AI model, and persistently saving the chat logs to local JSON files in a `./chats` directory.

### Tools (`src/harness/tools/`)
* **`all-tools.ts`**: An aggregation file that exports an array of all available tools to make registering them straightforward.
* **`tool.ts`**: Defines the abstract base `Tool` class. It enforces the structure that all tools must follow (like requiring a `description`, `id`, and a `call` method) and holds the regular expression used to parse tool calls from the model's output.
* **`list-dir.ts`**: Implements the `list-dir` tool, allowing the AI to inspect directories and see their contents (files and folders).
* **`list-tools.ts`**: Implements the `list-tools` tool, returning descriptions and instructions for all the tools the AI has access to.
* **`read-file.ts`**: Implements the `read-file` tool, granting the AI the ability to read the text contents of files on the system.
* **`write-file.ts`**: Implements the `write-file` tool, which lets the AI write text to new or existing files on the file system.
